name: spin (spin::Mutex)
baseline: std::sync::Mutex on Linux (futex-based since 1.62; pthread-based in the 2020 run)
one_liner: Spin-based Mutex, RwLock and Once for no_std; with std available it trails std's futex Mutex under contention and ties or wins only when idle.

name: actix-web 4
baseline: axum with Tokio's default multi-threaded runtime: TechEmpower Round 22 entry (axum 0.6.16, hyper 0.14) and HttpArena 2026 standard-mode entry (axum 0.8)
one_liner: Mature Rust web framework that beats default-config axum 1.1-2.6x on small-request benchmarks; the lead shrinks to ~15% once a database is involved.

name: stretto (Rust port of Ristretto)
baseline: An LRU cache behind std::sync::Mutex (hashlink LruCache), plus QuickCache and Moka
one_liner: TinyLFU cache ported from Go's Ristretto; wins hit ratio only on small caches over skewed keys, and 0.8 measured broken.

name: fast-float (Eisel-Lemire float parsing)
baseline: std's str::parse::<f64> (FromStr)
one_liner: Port of Lemire's fast_float that beat std's float parsing 2-8x on Rust 1.49; std absorbed the algorithm in 1.55 and the gap is now 1.0x-1.3x.

name: lexical-core (number parsing and formatting)
baseline: std's str::parse::<f64> and Display for floats
one_liner: Configurable number parsing and formatting; 2.8x faster than std at printing floats, but no longer the fastest and only 1.1x-1.5x ahead at parsing.

name: ureq (blocking HTTP client)
baseline: reqwest 0.11.18 on a current-thread Tokio runtime, 1,000 sequential keep-alive GETs to a local server
one_liner: Blocking HTTP client with a small dependency tree; no measured speed advantage over reqwest for sequential requests.

name: parking_lot (Mutex and RwLock)
baseline: std::sync::Mutex and RwLock on Linux; the README claim was measured against the pre-1.62 pthread-based std locks
one_liner: Compact adaptive Mutex and RwLock whose old '5x faster than std' claim predates std's futex locks; today std wins under heavy contention.

name: buffa (protobuf with zero-copy view types)
baseline: prost 0.14 decoding into and encoding from owned generated structs
one_liner: Pure-Rust protobuf with editions support; about even with prost on owned types, 1.1-2.8x faster decode through zero-copy views.

name: wincode (bincode-compatible serializer)
baseline: bincode 1.3.3 through serde (same wire format)
one_liner: Drop-in for bincode 1's wire format that serializes 3x-33x and deserializes 1.1x-26x faster than bincode 1.3.3 through serde.

name: arrow-rs `simd` feature (hand-written packed_simd arithmetic kernels)
baseline: arrow's scalar arithmetic kernels left to LLVM's auto-vectorizer
one_liner: Arrow's hand-written packed_simd kernels lost to auto-vectorized scalar loops (1.5-2.1x slower) and were removed; the default won.

name: quick_cache (S3-FIFO concurrent cache)
baseline: An LRU cache behind std::sync::Mutex (hashlink LruCache), and Mini Moka
one_liner: Sharded S3-FIFO cache: up to 5.5x the hit ratio of Mutex<LRU> at similar per-op cost, about 4x faster than Mini Moka.

name: async-std
baseline: Tokio master of early November 2019 (already on the rewritten multi-threaded scheduler)
one_liner: Discontinued std-like async runtime whose 2019 launch microbenchmarks showed up to 1.95x faster task spawning than Tokio.

name: crc-fast (SIMD CRC-16/32/64 for all catalogued variants)
baseline: crc crate 3.x with its default bytewise table (about 0.5 GiB/s)
one_liner: SIMD CRC for every CRC-16/32/64 variant, reaching ~111 GiB/s on AVX-512 servers; the '>220X' headline compares against crc's slowest default.

name: aws-lc-rs (AWS-LC with a ring-compatible API)
baseline: RustCrypto aes-gcm 0.11.1, p256 0.14.0, p384 0.14.0 and rsa 0.10.0-rc.19 on x86_64
one_liner: Rust bindings to AWS-LC with ring's API: 3.2x RustCrypto's AES-GCM throughput and 10x its RSA-2048 signing rate on a Ryzen 9 7940HS.

name: glam (SIMD 3D math types)
baseline: nalgebra 0.35.0 small fixed-size f32 vectors, matrices and transforms
one_liner: 3D math library with SIMD-backed Vec4/Mat4/Quat; 2-12x faster than nalgebra on matrix and transform ops, slower on some vector ops.

name: blake3 (BLAKE3 hash)
license: CC0-1.0 OR Apache-2.0 OR Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception
baseline: SHA-256 (OpenSSL in the published chart); the Rust default is the sha2 crate, which uses SHA-NI or ARMv8 SHA2 instructions when the CPU has them
one_liner: BLAKE3 hash: 14x SHA-256 on a 2019 AVX-512 server without SHA-NI, but slower than hardware SHA-256 on short inputs.

name: sold (mold fork for macOS)
baseline: Apple's default macOS linker called through cc: ld-prime with Xcode 15 or later, ld64 before that
one_liner: Archived macOS fork of mold; its author now points users to Apple's Xcode 15+ linker, which is already the default.

name: smartstring (SmartString inline string)
baseline: String for short strings
one_liner: Archived inline-string String replacement; it saves allocations, but an independent benchmark drops it from access tests for being slow.

name: ring (BoringSSL-derived crypto primitives)
baseline: RustCrypto aes-gcm 0.11.1, p256 0.14.0 and rsa 0.10.0-rc.19 on x86_64; aes-gcm 0.10.3 on Apple M2
one_liner: Rust API over BoringSSL's assembly: about 3x RustCrypto's AES-GCM throughput and 8x its ECDSA P-256 signing rate on a Ryzen 9 7940HS.

name: indexset (two-level order-statistic B-tree)
baseline: std::collections::BTreeSet and BTreeMap
one_liner: Ordered set and map built from fixed-capacity Vec leaves; faster scans and rank lookups than std's BTreeMap, slower point lookups and removals.

name: bstr (byte strings with reusable Finder and line iteration)
baseline: std line-by-line search: BufRead::read_line into a String, then str::contains
one_liner: Byte-string extension traits for &[u8]; a line-by-line grep ran 2.8x faster than String plus str::contains, measured before Rust 1.67.

name: memchr (memchr::memmem substring search)
baseline: std substring search (str::find / str::contains: Two-Way plus the SSE2 short-needle path) on rustc 1.73.0-nightly
one_liner: SIMD substring search for &[u8] that runs about 5x to 6x faster than std's str::find across 53 benchmarks.

name: pcre2 (Rust bindings to PCRE2 with JIT)
baseline: regex 1.12.2
one_liner: Rust bindings to PCRE2; the JIT wins some rebar workloads but is about 2x slower than the regex crate overall.

name: snap (pure-Rust Snappy)
baseline: Snappy C++ 1.1.8 through the same benchmark harness
one_liner: Pure-Rust Snappy with raw and frame formats; measured within about 10% of C++ Snappy either way on x86_64.

name: wtx (gRPC server)
baseline: tonic (rust_tonic_mt and rust_tonic_st entries in grpc_bench, unary RPC)
one_liner: Collection of web transports with its own HTTP/2 and gRPC stack; beat tonic in its author's grpc_bench run, lost by ~1.8x in the maintainer's.

name: redb (copy-on-write B+tree KV store)
baseline: RocksDB (rust-rocksdb 0.22) and SQLite (rusqlite 0.37, bundled, default rollback journal) as key-value stores
one_liner: Pure-Rust ACID key-value store; 2.6x faster reads and single commits than RocksDB, but slower batch writes and larger files.

name: sonic-rs (SIMD JSON parser and serializer)
baseline: serde_json::from_str / to_string (serde_json version at the time of the README run, not stated)
one_liner: ByteDance's SIMD JSON library; its own runs parse 1.7x-2.3x (structs) and 3.4x-5.2x (untyped) faster than serde_json with target-cpu=native.

name: crossbeam-channel
baseline: std::sync::mpsc before Rust 1.67; since 1.67 std::sync::mpsc wraps a copy of this implementation
one_liner: Multi-producer multi-consumer channels with select!; its speed lead over std::sync::mpsc ended when std adopted its implementation in Rust 1.67.

name: fast_image_resize (SIMD image resizing)
baseline: image 0.25.6 resize (imageops) on the same images and filters
one_liner: SIMD image resizer that downsizes 5-27x faster than the image crate's resize, depending on filter, pixel format and CPU.

name: flexon (SIMD JSON parser)
baseline: serde_json 1.0.151 deserializing typed structs
one_liner: Young SIMD JSON parser with serde support; an independent benchmark has it deserializing 1.5x-1.9x faster than serde_json.

name: const-hex
baseline: hex 0.4.3 encode/decode, and std formatting with write!(f, "{byte:02x}") per byte
one_liner: Drop-in replacement for the hex crate with SIMD and const-eval, measured 6x-99x faster than hex and up to 158x faster than std formatting.

name: glommio (io_uring thread-per-core runtime)
baseline: Tokio 1.14 multi-threaded runtime with one worker per core (current_thread at 1 core), serving the same TCP ping-pong server
one_liner: Datadog's thread-per-core io_uring runtime; 1.4-2.3x Tokio's peak QPS at 4-16 cores in a third-party 2021 echo benchmark, slower on one core.

name: Diesel (sync ORM and query builder)
baseline: sqlx 0.8 PostgreSQL driver (query_as! macro)
one_liner: Rust ORM with compile-time checked queries; loads 10,000-row results 1.2x to 1.4x faster than sqlx, ties it on single rows.

name: itoa (integer-to-string)
baseline: std's Display for integers (format!, to_string, write!)
one_liner: Integer-to-decimal formatting without core::fmt::Formatter; std 1.98's NumBuffer::format_into now offers the same path built in.

name: ryu (Ryū float-to-string)
baseline: std's Display for f32/f64
one_liner: Ryū shortest float-to-string: 2.2x-2.4x faster than std's float Display, now overtaken by zmij.

name: zmij (Żmij float-to-string)
baseline: std's Display for f64 (format!, to_string, write!)
one_liner: Rust port of Victor Zverovich's Żmij float printer: 8x-11x faster than std's float Display and about 4x faster than ryu.

name: zero-postgres (sync and async PostgreSQL client)
baseline: tokio-postgres, sqlx and Diesel on PostgreSQL
one_liner: New PostgreSQL client that tops Diesel's select benchmarks: 1.3x faster than tokio-postgres, about 2x sqlx on 10,000 rows.

name: rpmalloc (rpmalloc-rs global allocator)
baseline: glibc 2.43 malloc on Linux
one_liner: Rust wrapper for rpmalloc, a thread-caching allocator; upstream beats glibc on most 2026 benchmarks, but the crate bundles a 2022-era snapshot.

name: zune-jpeg (JPEG decoder)
baseline: jpeg-decoder 0.3, the image crate's JPEG decoder before image 0.25
one_liner: Pure-Rust JPEG decoder, 1.5-2x faster than jpeg-decoder per its author; it is now the image crate's default JPEG decoder.

name: zune-png (PNG decoder)
baseline: png 0.18 (image-rs/png), the image crate's PNG decoder
one_liner: Pure-Rust PNG/APNG decoder; faster than the png crate on 8-bit and interlaced images, slower on 16-bit and palette images.

name: kanal
baseline: std::sync::mpsc (Rust 1.85.1, crossbeam-based) and crossbeam-channel
one_liner: MPMC channel with sync and async APIs that leads most of its own 2025 charts against std mpsc and crossbeam, though not bounded SPSC.

name: fjall (pure-Rust LSM-tree)
baseline: RocksDB through rust-rocksdb 0.22, with an LRU block cache and bloom filters
one_liner: Pure-Rust LSM-tree engine; beats RocksDB on batch writes and reads in one comparison, builds in seconds, compacts worse.

name: xitca-web (HTTP library and web framework)
baseline: axum 0.7.9 on hyper 1.x and Tokio, TechEmpower Round 23 entries (axum for plaintext/JSON, axum-pg for fortunes)
one_liner: Rust web framework with its own HTTP stack; ahead of axum on pipelined plaintext in TechEmpower, level on JSON and fortunes.

name: rapidhash (wyhash successor)
baseline: std HashMap's RandomState (SipHash-1-3)
one_liner: Portable rapidhash/wyhash-family hasher with randomized secrets; about 5x faster than SipHash-1-3 and slightly ahead of foldhash.

name: hyper (raw server, without axum)
baseline: axum on the same hyper and Tokio stack (TechEmpower Round 23: axum 0.7.9; HttpArena 2026: axum 0.8 standard mode)
one_liner: Serving straight from hyper beats axum 1.4-3.5x on trivial handlers, but the gap is 6% on JSON and reverses on TechEmpower fortunes.

name: papaya (lock-free read-optimized hash map)
baseline: RwLock<HashMap>, and dashmap as the common concurrent alternative
one_liner: Lock-free concurrent hash table where reads never block; aimed at read-heavy workloads and predictable latency.

name: fdeflate (safe-Rust inflate, PNG-tuned)
baseline: flate2 1.1 with its default miniz_oxide backend, streaming inflate in 4096-byte chunks
one_liner: Safe-Rust deflate decoder from image-rs; inflated 1.5x to 1.6x faster than miniz_oxide in a flate2 prototype.

name: image 0.25: JPEG decoding switched to zune-jpeg
baseline: image 0.24 and earlier, which decoded JPEG with jpeg-decoder
one_liner: Since 0.25.0 the image crate decodes JPEG with zune-jpeg instead of jpeg-decoder; upgrading gets the 1.5-2x faster decoder for free.

name: evmap (left-right eventually consistent map)
baseline: RwLock<HashMap> (parking_lot RwLock around std HashMap in the measurements)
one_liner: Eventually consistent multi-value map built on left-right; lock-free reads that scale, at the cost of slow, batched writes.

name: flurry (port of Java's ConcurrentHashMap)
baseline: RwLock<HashMap> (parking_lot RwLock around std HashMap in the measurements)
one_liner: Rust port of Java's ConcurrentHashMap; scales on reads but has memory and write-throughput problems its author acknowledges.

name: ruzstd (pure-Rust zstd)
baseline: The zstd crate's bindings to the C reference zstd library
one_liner: Pure-Rust zstd decoder and partial encoder; 1.4x to 3.5x slower than the C library behind the zstd crate.

name: cargo-pgo (profile-guided optimization)
baseline: cargo build --release with no profile data
one_liner: Cargo subcommand that automates profile-guided optimization; PGO made rustc itself 10-20% faster in several measurements.

name: BOLT post-link optimization (via cargo-pgo)
baseline: A PGO-optimized release binary without BOLT
one_liner: Profile-driven code layout applied after linking; adds roughly 2-6% on top of PGO in rustc measurements, at a size cost.

name: speedy (binary serialization)
baseline: bincode 1.3.3 through serde
one_liner: Fast custom-derive binary serializer, 3x-34x faster than bincode 1.3 to serialize, but unmaintained and dropped from the main benchmark.

name: voracious_radix_sort (MSD/LSD radix sorts)
baseline: slice::sort_unstable (pdqsort) and slice::sort before Rust 1.81
one_liner: Radix sorts for Rust primitives and keyed structs; about 3x faster than pre-1.81 sort_unstable on a million u64.

name: libdeflater (libdeflate bindings)
baseline: flate2 with no feature flags in 2019 (the README calls it the miniz implementation; miniz_oxide results sit on a separate branch), whole-buffer compress and decompress
one_liner: Bindings to libdeflate for whole-buffer gzip/zlib; 2019 README shows 2-3x over flate2's old C miniz default.

name: LLVM lld for macOS (ld64.lld)
baseline: Apple ld-prime, the default linker with Xcode 15 or later, called through cc
one_liner: LLVM's Mach-O linker: once 4x faster than Apple's ld64, now slower than Apple's ld-prime default on Apple silicon.

name: wide (f32x4/f32x8 SIMD types, measured through ultraviolet and nalgebra/simba AoSoA types)
baseline: Scalar per-element math with glam 0.34.1 (one Vec3/Mat4 at a time) doing the same total work
one_liner: Stable-Rust SIMD vector types; AoSoA math built on them runs 4-12x faster than one-at-a-time glam in mathbench, with target-cpu=native.

name: json-rust (json crate, DOM parser)
baseline: serde_json 1.0.72, both serde_json::Value (DOM) and typed struct parsing
one_liner: Untyped JSON DOM crate that beat serde_json's Value in a 2021 run but not serde_json struct parsing; unmaintained since 2020.

name: base64 0.23 (Simd engine)
baseline: base64's scalar GeneralPurpose engine (general_purpose::STANDARD, the only engine through 0.22 and still the prelude default in 0.23)
one_liner: The base64 crate's own SIMD engine (0.23+): 3.7x faster encode and up to 7.1x faster decode than its scalar engine, if you opt in.

name: once_cell (sync::Lazy)
baseline: lazy_static 1.4 (lazy_static! macro)
one_liner: Lazy statics without a macro, now mostly in std as OnceLock and LazyLock; access speed matches lazy_static, so pick it for API, not speed.

name: simd-csv (SIMD CSV reader)
baseline: the csv crate's Reader (csv 1.x)
one_liner: CSV reader that pairs a state machine with SIMD byte searching; its author measures up to 4x-6x over the csv crate on long-cell data.

name: heed (LMDB bindings)
baseline: RocksDB (rust-rocksdb 0.22) and SQLite (rusqlite 0.37, bundled, default rollback journal) as key-value stores
one_liner: Typed Rust wrapper over LMDB; fastest reads in redb's comparison, 4.6x RocksDB, but slower batch writes and 3x the disk.

name: zld (faster fork of Apple ld64)
baseline: Apple's default macOS linker called through cc: ld-prime with Xcode 15 or later, ld64 when zld was current
one_liner: Archived fork of Apple's old ld64 that claimed links at least 40% faster; Xcode 15's ld-prime replaced the linker it improved on.

name: snmalloc-rs (snmalloc global allocator)
baseline: glibc 2.43 malloc on Linux
one_liner: Rust bindings for Microsoft's message-passing allocator; 7.2x faster than glibc on cross-thread frees and 4-18% faster on real programs.

name: moka (TinyLFU concurrent cache, with Mini Moka)
baseline: An LRU cache behind std::sync::Mutex (hashlink LruCache)
one_liner: Caffeine-style cache with TTL and listeners; 4.5x the hit ratio of Mutex<LRU> on a search trace, but 7.3x the per-op cost.

name: monoio (io_uring thread-per-core runtime)
baseline: Tokio 1.14 multi-threaded runtime with one worker per core (current_thread at 1 core), serving the same TCP ping-pong server
one_liner: Thread-per-core io_uring runtime from ByteDance; 2-3x Tokio's peak QPS on a 4-16 core echo server in its 2021 benchmark.

name: sccache (shared compilation cache)
baseline: cargo build with no shared cache: every machine or CI job recompiles every dependency
one_liner: Compiler-output cache that wraps rustc; helps clean CI builds of dependencies but cannot cache binaries, proc macros or incremental crates.

name: borsh (Binary Object Representation Serializer for Hashing)
baseline: bincode 1.3.3 through serde
one_liner: Canonical binary format from NEAR for hashing and consensus; benchmarks at the same speed as bincode 1.3, not faster.

name: faster-hex
baseline: hex 0.4.3 (hex::encode / hex::decode)
one_liner: SIMD hex encoding and decoding, measured 6x-71x faster than the hex crate by a third party.

name: cargo-nextest (test runner)
baseline: cargo test (libtest), which runs test binaries one after another
one_liner: Test runner that runs every test in its own process from one global pool; 1.4x-3.4x faster than cargo test on nine real projects.

name: ntex (web framework, actix-web fork)
baseline: axum on hyper and Tokio: TechEmpower Round 23 entry (axum 0.7.9, one current-thread runtime per core) and HttpArena 2026 standard-mode entry (axum 0.8, default multi-threaded runtime)
one_liner: actix-style web framework that beats default-config axum 1.3-2.2x on HttpArena but is within 2-9% of thread-per-core axum on TechEmpower.

name: base64-simd
baseline: the base64 crate's scalar engine (version not stated in the dashboard)
one_liner: SIMD base64 encoder/decoder; 6x-8.5x faster than the base64 crate in 2023, a gap base64 0.23's own SIMD engine has mostly closed.

name: hex-simd
baseline: hex 0.4 (hex::encode / hex::decode)
one_liner: SIMD hex encoder/decoder measured 18x-23x faster than the hex crate on 1-4 KiB inputs by its author.

name: gxhash (AES/SIMD hasher)
baseline: std HashMap's RandomState (SipHash-1-3)
one_liner: AES- and SIMD-based hasher that is fastest on long keys but slower than foldhash or rapidhash on integers, and needs AES at build time.

name: foldhash (folded-multiply hasher, hashbrown's default)
baseline: std HashMap's RandomState (SipHash-1-3)
one_liner: Portable, seeded hasher built on a folded multiply; about 5x faster than SipHash-1-3 across hash-table workloads.

name: glidesort (stable hybrid merge/quick sort)
baseline: slice::sort and sort_unstable as of rustc 1.69 nightly (before driftsort and ipnsort)
one_liner: Stable sort mixing powersort run merging with stable quicksort; its ideas now ship in std's driftsort, which narrows the gap.

name: compact_str (CompactString, 24-byte inline string)
baseline: String for short strings
one_liner: Mutable String replacement that stores strings up to 24 bytes inline in the same 24 bytes; avoids allocations for short strings.

name: lz4_flex (pure-Rust LZ4)
baseline: lz4 1.9.3 C library through the lzzz bindings, block format
one_liner: Pure-Rust LZ4 that matches the C library when unsafe features are on; the default safe build is up to 20% slower than C.

name: mimalloc (global allocator)
baseline: System allocator: musl's malloc in static musl builds; glibc 2.43 malloc on Linux
one_liner: Rust global allocator for Microsoft's mimalloc: 25x faster than musl's malloc in a 48-core test, 4-54% faster than glibc on most real programs.

name: rayon (work-stealing data parallelism)
baseline: Sequential code on one thread; the catalog default (std::thread with hand-split work) was not measured
one_liner: Work-stealing parallel iterators and join; its published speedups are against sequential code, not against hand-split std::thread.

name: rkyv (zero-copy deserialization)
baseline: bincode 1.3.3 through serde (full deserialize into owned types)
one_liner: Zero-copy archive format: reads data in place in nanoseconds instead of deserializing, and serializes plain-data arrays 35x faster than bincode 1.3.

name: leapfrog (LeapMap concurrent hash map)
baseline: RwLock<HashMap> (parking_lot RwLock around std HashMap)
one_liner: Lock-free concurrent map using leapfrog probing; about 12x RwLock<HashMap> throughput at 16 threads on reads, with value-type restrictions.

name: mold (ELF linker)
baseline: rust-lld, the default linker on x86_64 Linux since Rust 1.90; GNU ld through cc on other Linux targets
one_liner: Parallel ELF linker by lld's original author; links large programs several times faster than lld and far faster than GNU ld.

name: rusqlite (synchronous SQLite driver)
baseline: sqlx 0.8 async SQLite driver (query_as! macro and query + FromRow)
one_liner: Synchronous SQLite bindings; queries ran 11x to 49x faster than sqlx's async SQLite driver in Diesel's nightly suite.

name: rusqlite bulk inserts (cached prepared statements, multi-row batches, one transaction)
baseline: rusqlite inserting one row per execute call in a loop, with the same SQLite PRAGMAs
one_liner: Batching SQLite inserts through rusqlite's cached prepared statements cut 100M inserts from about 3 minutes to 34 seconds.

name: hashbrown crate (SwissTable with foldhash as default hasher)
baseline: std::collections::HashMap, which has used the same hashbrown table since Rust 1.36 but defaults to SipHash-1-3
one_liner: The SwissTable crate behind std's HashMap; on today's toolchains its speed edge over std is only its foldhash default hasher.

name: zlib-ng via flate2 (libz-ng-sys backend)
baseline: flate2 1.1 with its default miniz_oxide backend, streaming inflate and deflate in 4096-byte chunks
one_liner: flate2's zlib-ng C backend: level-6 deflate 2.1x to 2.7x faster than miniz_oxide; inflate gains are small to none.

name: regex 1.9+ (regex-automata meta engine rewrite)
baseline: regex 1.7.3, the last release before the internals were rebuilt on regex-automata
one_liner: The regex crate's 1.9 rewrite onto regex-automata: the default Rust regex engine searches about 1.5x faster on average than 1.7.

name: regex-lite (small, fast-building regex)
baseline: regex 1.9.0 with every feature disabled except std (build time and binary size); regex 1.12.2 for regex compile and search time
one_liner: Drop-in subset of the regex crate that builds in about 40% of the time and adds about a sixth of the binary size, at the cost of much slower searches.

name: smol_str (inline immutable string)
baseline: String for short, mostly immutable strings
one_liner: Immutable string type that stores up to 23 bytes inline and clones in O(1); far fewer allocations than String for short tokens.

name: rustc-hash (FxHasher, rewritten in 2.0)
baseline: std HashMap's RandomState (SipHash-1-3)
one_liner: The rustc compiler's unkeyed FxHasher; fastest on integer keys, with no DoS resistance and known collision patterns.

name: rustc_codegen_cranelift (Cranelift codegen backend)
baseline: cargo build (dev profile) with the default LLVM backend
one_liner: Nightly-only codegen backend that compiles debug builds 5-20% faster than LLVM by generating less optimized code.

name: tokio-postgres (async PostgreSQL driver)
baseline: sqlx 0.8 PostgreSQL driver (query_as! macro and query + FromRow)
one_liner: Async PostgreSQL driver; 1.5x to 1.9x faster than sqlx on 10,000-row results, slower on one-row queries in the same suite.

name: rand SmallRng (Xoshiro256++ on 64-bit)
baseline: rand's StdRng and ThreadRng / rand::rng() (ChaCha12)
one_liner: rand's non-cryptographic SmallRng: about 2.7x to 3.6x faster than the ChaCha12 generator behind StdRng and rand::rng().

name: RustCrypto asm-hashes (the sha2 'asm' feature)
baseline: sha2's built-in backends: portable Rust plus SHA-NI and ARMv8 SHA2 intrinsics selected at runtime
one_liner: Assembly SHA-1/SHA-2/MD5 compression functions for RustCrypto; archived and dropped from sha2 0.11 with no published speedup.

name: simdutf8 (SIMD UTF-8 validation)
baseline: std::str::from_utf8 (Rust 1.52.0 on x86_64, 1.54.0-nightly on aarch64)
one_liner: SIMD drop-in for std::str::from_utf8: up to 23x faster on valid non-ASCII text and up to 4x on ASCII for inputs of 64 bytes or more.

name: faer (dense linear algebra)
baseline: nalgebra (pure Rust, matrixmultiply backend) and ndarray with OpenBLAS, f64 column-major matrices
one_liner: Pure-Rust dense linear algebra; 5-13x faster than nalgebra on large decompositions, about even on matmul and slower on tiny matrices.

name: simd-json (SIMD JSON parser with a serde-style API)
baseline: serde_json 1.0.151 serializing and deserializing typed structs
one_liner: Rust port of simdjson with serde support; in an independent benchmark it deserializes 1.2x-1.5x and serializes about 1.6x faster than serde_json.

name: fastrand (wyrand PRNG)
baseline: rand's StdRng (ChaCha12, the algorithm behind ThreadRng and rand::rng()) and rand's SmallRng
one_liner: Small wyrand-based RNG: 0.51 ns per u64 against 4.11 ns for rand's StdRng and 1.13 ns for SmallRng on an M1 Max.

name: bitcode (compact binary Encode/Decode)
baseline: bincode 1.3.3 through serde; also serde_json 1.0.151
one_liner: Binary format with its own derive that serializes 4x-6x and deserializes 1.4x-2.9x faster than bincode 1.3 via serde, with smaller output.

name: sled (Bw-tree-style embedded KV store)
baseline: RocksDB through rust-rocksdb 0.22 (the LSM-tree its README compares itself to), and SQLite through rusqlite
one_liner: Lock-free embedded KV store whose LSM-like write claim fails: batch writes 1.9x slower than RocksDB, slowest bulk load tested.

name: crc32fast (SIMD CRC-32/IEEE)
baseline: crc crate 1.8.1 in the README table; today's crc 3.x defaults to a 256-entry table
one_liner: CRC-32/IEEE with runtime-selected PCLMULQDQ or ARMv8 CRC instructions; 7.3 GB/s in its own table, far ahead of table-driven CRC.

name: quick-protobuf (borrowing protobuf decoder)
baseline: prost (version at the time of the 2018 results; the perftest manifest now names prost 0.9.0)
one_liner: Protobuf crate whose generated types borrow strings and bytes from the input; 2018 numbers show faster reads than prost, slower writes.

name: tikv-jemallocator (jemalloc global allocator)
baseline: System allocator: macOS libmalloc (rustc builds), glibc 2.43 malloc, musl malloc
one_liner: Maintained jemalloc bindings that rustc itself uses; 13-14% faster rustc builds on macOS, mixed results against modern glibc.

name: aHash (AES-based keyed hasher)
baseline: std HashMap's RandomState (SipHash-1-3) for in-memory hash map keys
one_liner: Keyed, randomly seeded hasher for HashMap that uses AES instructions where available; several times faster than SipHash-1-3.

name: Tokio multi-threaded scheduler rewrite (2019)
baseline: Tokio's previous work-stealing thread pool (tokio-threadpool, the Tokio 0.1 scheduler)
one_liner: Tokio's 2019 scheduler rewrite, the basis of its multi-threaded runtime since 0.2; 12x on one microbenchmark, 34% on a Hyper server.

name: bzip2 0.6 (libbz2-rs-sys Rust backend)
baseline: The C libbzip2 that the bzip2 crate linked through bzip2-sys before 0.6.0
one_liner: bzip2 crate 0.6 swapped C libbzip2 for a Rust port: 10-15% fewer cycles to compress, 4-10% fewer to decompress.

name: zlib-rs (flate2 zlib-rs backend)
baseline: flate2 1.1 with its default miniz_oxide backend, streaming inflate and deflate in 4096-byte chunks
one_liner: Rust port of zlib-ng as a flate2 backend; inflates about 1.3x and deflates 1.9x to 2.6x faster than flate2's default miniz_oxide.

name: wild (ELF linker)
baseline: rust-lld, the default linker on x86_64 Linux since Rust 1.90
one_liner: Young Rust-written ELF linker aimed at fast iterative builds; beats lld where it works but trails mold and cannot link some large programs.

name: winnow (parser combinators)
baseline: nom 8.0.0 parser combinators
one_liner: Fork of nom that parsed canada.json 2.5x faster and built 3x faster than nom 8 in its author's comparison suite.

name: pajamax (synchronous gRPC server)
baseline: tonic (rust_tonic_mt entry in grpc_bench, unary RPC)
one_liner: Thread-per-connection gRPC server with a gRPC-specific HTTP/2 parser; 3-30% faster than tonic in a third-party run, not the 10x its author cites.

name: DashMap (sharded RwLock hash map)
baseline: RwLock<HashMap> (parking_lot RwLock around std HashMap in the measurements)
one_liner: Sharded concurrent HashMap with a HashMap-like &self API; scales far past RwLock<HashMap> under contention but is slower single-threaded.

name: may_minihttp (HTTP/1.1 server on stackful coroutines)
baseline: axum 0.7.9 on hyper 1.x and Tokio, TechEmpower Round 23 entries (axum for plaintext/JSON, axum-pg with tokio-postgres for fortunes)
one_liner: Minimal HTTP/1.1 server on the may coroutine runtime; tops TechEmpower plaintext but leads axum by only 14-19% on JSON and fortunes.

name: flume
baseline: std::sync::mpsc (the claim was charted against the pre-1.67 implementation)
one_liner: MPMC channel with sync and async APIs and no unsafe code; its 'always faster than std mpsc' chart predates std adopting crossbeam's design.

name: codegen-units = 1 in the release profile
baseline: cargo build --release with the default codegen-units = 16 and thin-local LTO
one_liner: Compiling each crate as one LLVM unit gains about 1.5-2% runtime and shrinks binaries, but roughly doubles release build time.

name: Less debug info in dev builds (debug = false or "line-tables-only")
baseline: cargo build with the dev profile's default debug = true (full debug info)
one_liner: Turning off or trimming debug info in Cargo's dev profile cuts incremental rebuild times by up to 30-40%.

name: rust-lld as the default linker on x86_64 Linux (Rust 1.90)
baseline: GNU ld (BFD) called through cc, the default linker for x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu before Rust 1.90
one_liner: Since Rust 1.90, rustc links x86_64 Linux programs with its bundled lld instead of GNU ld, which cuts link time several-fold.

name: Fat LTO (lto = "fat") in the release profile
baseline: cargo build --release with the defaults lto = false (thin-local LTO) and codegen-units = 16
one_liner: Whole-program LTO across all crates: single-digit runtime gains in the best measurement, at several times the release build time.

name: panic = "abort" in the release profile
baseline: cargo build --release with the default panic = "unwind"
one_liner: Aborting instead of unwinding on panic shrinks binaries; any runtime gain is described as slight and is unmeasured.

name: Parallel rustc front end (-Z threads)
baseline: cargo build with the default single-threaded rustc front end
one_liner: Nightly option that runs rustc's parsing, type checking and borrow checking on several threads; up to 50% faster builds.

name: PGO, LTO and BOLT in the official rustc builds
baseline: A rustc built with a plain release configuration, without PGO, LTO or BOLT
one_liner: The rustc you install with rustup is already built with PGO and LTO (and BOLT on x86_64 Linux), making it 10-30% faster than a plain build.

name: Pipelined compilation in Cargo (Rust 1.38)
baseline: Cargo before Rust 1.38, which waited for each dependency to finish compiling before starting crates that depend on it
one_liner: Since Rust 1.38, Cargo starts compiling a crate as soon as its dependencies' metadata is ready, not after they finish.

name: -C target-cpu=native
baseline: cargo build --release for the target's default generic CPU
one_liner: Compiling for the build machine's exact CPU helps vectorizable loops; for general code measured gains were nil or negative.

name: std HashMap and HashSet (hashbrown SwissTable, Rust 1.36)
baseline: std::collections::HashMap before Rust 1.36 (Robin Hood open addressing)
one_liner: Since Rust 1.36, std's HashMap is the hashbrown SwissTable, about 2x faster on lookups than the old Robin Hood table with the same hasher.

name: std float parsing (Eisel-Lemire, Rust 1.55)
baseline: std's float parsing before Rust 1.55 (dec2flt with Clinger's AlgorithmM and Bellerophon)
one_liner: Since Rust 1.55, str::parse::<f64> uses Eisel-Lemire and runs within about 1.2x of fast-float, down from 7x-8x behind.

name: std::simd (portable SIMD, nightly only)
baseline: Scalar Rust loops left to LLVM's auto-vectorizer (in the cited case, RangeSetBlaze::from_iter)
one_liner: Portable SIMD vector types in std; can beat auto-vectorized loops, but still nightly-only and with little published Rust benchmark data.

name: std slice::sort (driftsort, Rust 1.81)
baseline: slice::sort before Rust 1.81 (TimSort-style merge sort)
one_liner: Since Rust 1.81, slice::sort is driftsort: about 2.4x faster on random u64 and far faster on inputs with many duplicates.

name: std slice::sort_unstable (ipnsort, Rust 1.81)
baseline: slice::sort_unstable before Rust 1.81 (pdqsort)
one_liner: Since Rust 1.81, slice::sort_unstable is ipnsort: a faster, smaller pdqsort successor with a sorting-network small-sort.

name: std str::chars().count() word-at-a-time counting (Rust 1.60)
baseline: str::chars().count() before Rust 1.60
one_liner: Rust 1.60 made str::chars().count() about 4x to 5x faster on medium and large strings by counting a machine word at a time.

name: std str::contains SSE2 fast path for short needles (Rust 1.67)
baseline: str::contains(&str) before Rust 1.67, which used Two-Way for every needle length
one_liner: Rust 1.67 made str::contains with short needles 6x to 9x faster in long-haystack benchmarks on x86_64 by replacing Two-Way with an SSE2 scan.

name: std::sync::mpsc (crossbeam-channel implementation, Rust 1.67)
baseline: std::sync::mpsc before Rust 1.67: the original pre-1.0 implementation that upgraded between oneshot, stream and shared flavors at runtime
one_liner: Since Rust 1.67 std::sync::mpsc wraps a copy of crossbeam-channel, closing most of the gap that made crossbeam the default recommendation.

name: std::sync::Mutex and RwLock (futex-based, Rust 1.62)
baseline: std::sync::Mutex before Rust 1.62 on Linux: a heap-allocated pthread_mutex_t from glibc or musl
one_liner: Since Rust 1.62 std's Mutex, RwLock and Condvar on Linux are futex-based; the Mutex ran 2-4x faster than the pthread one it replaced in lock-bench.

name: std Vec growth skips capacities 1 and 2 (Rust 1.45)
baseline: Vec before Rust 1.45, whose push growth went 0, 1, 2, 4, 8
one_liner: Since Rust 1.45, a Vec grown by push starts at capacity 4 (8 for bytes) instead of 1, removing two reallocations for small Vecs.
